parts.visual:
A brilliant founder owns 60% of their company and thinks they are invincible. But during the Series B funding, they gave up 3 out of 5 seats on the Board of Directors to the VCs. One morning, the three VCs vote to fire the founder. The founder is escorted out of the building they built.

The Hierarchy:
1. The CEO is not the top. The CEO reports to the Board of Directors.
2. The Board's Job: The Board has a fiduciary duty to represent the shareholders. Their primary powers are hiring/firing the CEO, approving the annual budget, and approving the sale of the company.
parts.audio: When you take venture capital, you sell control of your destiny. The Board of Directors is the true sovereign power of a startup. If you do not control the board seats, you are merely an employee who can be fired at any time.

questions.question: A startup has a 5-person board: 2 Founders, 2 VCs, and 1 'Independent Director'. Why is the 'Independent Director' the most powerful person in the room?
options: Because they have the most money.

They are the tie-breaker. The founders will vote together, the VCs will vote together. In any major conflict (like whether to sell the company), the neutral Independent Director casts the deciding 3rd vote.
Because they own 100% of the stock.
questions.correct_answer: They are the tie-breaker. The founders will vote together, the VCs will vote together. In any major conflict (like whether to sell the company), the neutral Independent Director casts the deciding 3rd vote.
questions.explanation: Never let the VCs choose the Independent Director alone.

questions.question: Listen to the VC. What does 'Fiduciary Duty' mean in a legal context?
questions.tts_text: We like the founder personally. But he is refusing a $500 Million acquisition offer because he wants to build a 100-year legacy. As Board members, we have a legal obligation to maximize the financial return for the investors right now.
options: A legal mandate to act in the best financial interest of the shareholders, NOT the founder. If the Board ignores a massive payout to indulge the founder's ego, the shareholders can sue the Board.
questions.correct_answer: A legal mandate to act in the best financial interest of the shareholders, NOT the founder. If the Board ignores a massive payout to indulge the founder's ego, the shareholders can sue the Board.

questions.question: Can the Board of Directors dictate what color the startup's new logo should be?
options: No. The Board governs 'Strategy and Governance' (Budgets, M&A, hiring the CEO). The CEO governs 'Operations' (Marketing, Product, HR). If a Board is debating logo colors, it is a profoundly dysfunctional board.
questions.correct_answer: No. The Board governs 'Strategy and Governance' (Budgets, M&A, hiring the CEO). The CEO governs 'Operations' (Marketing, Product, HR). If a Board is debating logo colors, it is a profoundly dysfunctional board.

questions.question: What is a 'Board Observer'?
options: Usually a junior VC who is allowed to sit in the board meetings, listen to the highly confidential strategies, and participate in discussions, but legally has absolutely no voting power.
questions.correct_answer: Usually a junior VC who is allowed to sit in the board meetings, listen to the highly confidential strategies, and participate in discussions, but legally has absolutely no voting power.
questions.explanation: Be careful: observers don't vote, but they talk, and talk influences votes.
